key_insight: LuxRemix decomposes complex indoor illumination from a single multi-view capture into individual light sources, enabling independent per-light edits (on/off, chromaticity, intensity) while producing multi-view consistent results. This lets users interactively remix lighting without full geometry or expensive capture rigs.
problem_solved: Interactive, per-light editing and relighting of indoor scenes from limited captures is difficult because indoor illumination is complex, lights overlap, and edits must remain consistent across multiple views; existing methods struggle to isolate and controllably modify individual sources while preserving multi-view harmony.
method: Generative image-based light decomposition that factorizes scene illumination into constituent light sources from a single multi-view capture.
Per-light manipulation module that supports state (on/off), chromaticity, and intensity edits applied to the decomposed light components.
Multi-view lighting harmonization to reconcile edits across viewpoints and produce photometrically and geometrically coherent re-renderings.
impact: Provides a practical tool for content creators, AR/VR developers, and vision researchers to edit and study indoor lighting from modest captures, improving workflows for relighting, data augmentation, and controllable scene synthesis. It reduces capture complexity while enabling fine-grained lighting control.
visual_elements: Before/After multi-view scene panels showing original capture vs per-light edited results (toggle a lamp on/off, change color).
Pipeline diagram: multi-view input → light decomposition → per-light controls → remix → harmonized output.
UI mockup with sliders/colour wheels for per-light intensity and chromaticity plus on/off toggles.
Multi-view consistency visualization (heatmap or side-by-side views) showing harmonization reducing artifacts across camera views.
paper_title: LuxRemix: Lighting Decomposition and Remixing for Indoor Scenes
paper_authors: Ruofan Liang, Norman Müller, Ethan Weber, Duncan Zauss, Nandita Vijaykumar
